title: Graph Relationv0.1.0
description: A directed relation (edge) between two nodes in a linked graph. The relation's UUID identity is its key in the enclosing `relations` dictionary — the object itself carries no `id` field. The relation classifies the relationship with a predicate string and names source and target nodes by their UUIDs. Arbitrary application-specific properties are carried in the optional `metadata` object. Relations are always directed (source → target); undirected relationships can be modelled by convention in `predicate` or by creating two opposing relations.

predicate.description: String describing the directed relationship between source and target. May be a plain application-defined string (e.g. "adjacentTo", "connectedBy") or a contexted compact IRI (e.g. "geo:sfWithin", "dcterms:isPartOf", "prov:wasDerivedFrom") whose prefix is declared in the document `context`. The schema enforces only that the value is a non-empty string; term validity for a contexted predicate is governed by the namespace's `vocabulary` (ontology), not by JSON Schema.

source.description: UUID of the source node at the tail of this directed relation. Referential integrity — that this UUID exists as a key in the graph's `nodes` dictionary — cannot be enforced by JSON Schema and MUST be verified at the application layer.

target.description: UUID of the target node at the head of this directed relation. Same referential integrity caveat as `source` applies.

metadata.description: Optional key-value map of application-specific relation properties (e.g. weight, label, timestamp, confidence). Each value is a value object ({value, type?, language?, direction?, unit?}) — see objects.schema.json#/$defs/value. Keys may be contexted compact IRIs whose prefix is declared in the document `context`.
